items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: And all the guys would be in. Billy Eckstine. And Gerry Gray, Wardell's wife, would be there.

ctx.x: worked before-hours and after-hours. And he had his big car, and he dressed, he was real dapper and everything. And the guy knew nothing about the saxophone, but he was one of the busiest guys in town. All he would do was blow into the horn and just work his fingers, and bow his body up and down to whatever was... Everything meant the same to him, you know.
And all the guys would be in. Billy Eckstine. And Gerry Gray, Wardell's wife, would be there. They used to really put him on, you know.

And so, I'll never forget the first night he heard Charlie Parker. He had been hearing about Charlie Parker, that Charlie Parker was in town, and everybody was laying for him to walk in because Charlie Parker was on the stand. So we were up on the stand, and Charlie Parker was right in the middle of his solo playing "Cherokee." And when Will Roland came in, he headed straight for the bandstand. You know, he wanted to get to Charlie Parker, you know. And Billy Eckstine was eggin' him on. "Hey, Roland, all right,…
